NKJV.1: Moreover Job continued his discourse, and said:
NKJV.2: “As God lives, who has taken away my justice, And the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
NKJV.3: As long as my breath is in me, And the breath of God in my nostrils,
NKJV.4: My lips will not speak wickedness, Nor my tongue utter deceit.
NKJV.5: Far be it from me That I should say you are right; Till I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
NKJV.6: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go; My heart shall not reproach me as long as I live.
NKJV.7: “May my enemy be like the wicked, And he who rises up against me like the unrighteous.
NKJV.8: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, Though he may gain much, If God takes away his life?
NKJV.9: Will God hear his cry When trouble comes upon him?
NKJV.10: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? Will he always call on God?
NKJV.11: “I will teach you about the hand of God; What is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
NKJV.12: Surely all of you have seen it; Why then do you behave with complete nonsense?
NKJV.13: “This  is the portion of a wicked man with God, And the heritage of oppressors, received from the Almighty:
NKJV.14: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword; And his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
NKJV.15: Those who survive him shall be buried in death, And their widows shall not weep,
NKJV.16: Though he heaps up silver like dust, And piles up clothing like clay—
NKJV.17: He may pile it up, but the just will wear it, And the innocent will divide the silver.
NKJV.18: He builds his house like a moth, Like a booth which a watchman makes.
NKJV.19: The rich man will lie down, But not be gathered up; He opens his eyes, And he is no more.
NKJV.20: Terrors overtake him like a flood; A tempest steals him away in the night.
NKJV.21: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; It sweeps him out of his place.
NKJV.22: It hurls against him and does not spare; He flees desperately from its power.
NKJV.23: Men shall clap their hands at him, And shall hiss him out of his place.

NASB.1: Then Job continued his discourse and said,
NASB.2: 'As God lives, who has taken away my right, And the Almighty, who has embittered my soul,
NASB.3: For as long as life is in me, And the breath of God is in my nostrils,
NASB.4: My lips certainly will not speak unjustly, Nor will my tongue mutter deceit.
NASB.5: 'Far be it from me that I should declare you right; Till I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
NASB.6: 'I hold fast my righteousness and will not let it go. My heart does not reproach any of my days.
NASB.7: 'May my enemy be as the wicked And my opponent as the unjust.
NASB.8: 'For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, When God requires his life?
NASB.9: 'Will God hear his cry When distress comes upon him?
NASB.10: 'Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
NASB.11: 'I will instruct you in the power of God; What is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
NASB.12: 'Behold, all of you have seen [it]; Why then do you act foolishly?
NASB.13: 'This is the portion of a wicked man from God, And the inheritance [which] tyrants receive from the Almighty.
NASB.14: 'Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; And his descendants will not be satisfied with bread.
NASB.15: 'His survivors will be buried because of the plague, And their widows will not be able to weep.
NASB.16: 'Though he piles up silver like dust And prepares garments as [plentiful as] the clay,
NASB.17: He may prepare [it], but the just will wear [it] And the innocent will divide the silver.
NASB.18: 'He has built his house like the spider's web, Or as a hut [which] the watchman has made.
NASB.19: 'He lies down rich, but never again; He opens his eyes, and it is no longer.
NASB.20: 'Terrors overtake him like a flood; A tempest steals him away in the night.
NASB.21: 'The east wind carries him away, and he is gone, For it whirls him away from his place.
NASB.22: 'For it will hurl at him without sparing; He will surely try to flee from its power.
NASB.23: '[Men] will clap their hands at him And will hiss him from his place.

NLT.2:
“I vow by the living God, who has taken away my rights,
by the Almighty who has embittered my soul —
NLT.3:
As long as I live,
while I have breath from God,
NLT.4:
my lips will speak no evil,
and my tongue will speak no lies.
NLT.5:
I will never concede that you are right;
I will defend my integrity until I die.
NLT.6:
I will maintain my innocence without wavering.
My conscience is clear for as long as I live.
NLT.7:
“May my enemy be punished like the wicked,
my adversary like those who do evil.
NLT.8:
For what hope do the godless have when God cuts them off
and takes away their life?
NLT.9:
Will God listen to their cry
when trouble comes upon them?
NLT.10:
Can they take delight in the Almighty?
Can they call to God at any time?
NLT.11:
I will teach you about God’s power.
I will not conceal anything concerning the Almighty.
NLT.12:
But you have seen all this,
yet you say all these useless things to me.
NLT.13:
“This is what the wicked will receive from God;
this is their inheritance from the Almighty.
NLT.14:
They may have many children,
but the children will die in war or starve to death.
NLT.15:
Those who survive will die of a plague,
and not even their widows will mourn them.
NLT.16:
“Evil people may have piles of money
and may store away mounds of clothing.

But the righteous will wear that clothing,
and the innocent will divide that money.
NLT.18:
The wicked build houses as fragile as a spider’s web,

but wake to find that all their wealth is gone.
NLT.20:

and they are blown away in the storms of the night.
NLT.21:
The east wind carries them away, and they are gone.
It sweeps them away.
NLT.22:
It whirls down on them without mercy.
They struggle to flee from its power.
NLT.23:

and mocks them.

AMP.1: Job continued his discourse and said,
AMP.2:
"As God lives, who has taken away my right and denied me justice,
And the Almighty, who has caused bitterness and grief for my soul,
AMP.3:
As long as my life is within me,
And the breath of God is [still] in my nostrils,
AMP.4:
My lips will not speak unjustly,
Nor will my tongue utter deceit.
AMP.5:
"Far be it from me that I should admit you are right [in your accusations against me];
Until I die, I will not remove my integrity from me.
AMP.6:
"I hold fast my uprightness and my right standing with God and I will not let them go;
My heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
AMP.7:
"May my enemy be as the wicked,
And he who rises up against me be as the unrighteous (unjust).
AMP.8:
"For what is the hope of the godless, even though he has gained [in this world],
When God takes his life?
AMP.9:
"Will God hear his cry
When trouble and distress come upon him?
AMP.10:
"Will he take delight in the Almighty?
Will he call on God at all times?
AMP.11:
"I will teach you regarding the hand (power) of God;
I will not conceal what is with the Almighty [God's actual treatment of the wicked].
AMP.12:
"Behold, all of you have seen it;
Why then do you act vainly and foolishly [cherishing worthless concepts]?
AMP.13:
"This [which I am about to explain] is the portion of a wicked man from God,
And the inheritance which tyrants and oppressors receive from the Almighty:
AMP.14:
"Though his children are many, they are destined for the sword;
And his descendants will not have sufficient bread.
AMP.15:
"Those who survive him will be buried because of the plague,
And [their] widows will not be able to weep.
AMP.16:
"Though he heaps up silver like dust
And piles up clothing like clay,
AMP.17:
He may prepare it, but the just will wear it
And the innocent will divide the silver.
AMP.18:
"He builds his house like a spider's web,
Like a (temporary) hut which a watchman makes.
AMP.19:
"He lies down rich, but never will again;
He opens his eyes, and it is gone.
AMP.20:
"Terrors overtake him like a [suddenly rising] flood;
A windstorm steals him away in the night.
AMP.21:
"The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone;
It sweeps him out of his place.
AMP.22:
"For it will hurl [thunderbolts of God's wrath] at him unsparingly and without compassion;
He flees in haste from its power.
AMP.23:
"People will clap their hands at him [to mock and ridicule him]
And hiss him out of his place.

MSG.1: Having waited for Zophar, Job now resumed his defense:
MSG.2:
"God-Alive! He's denied me justice!
God Almighty! He's ruined my life!
MSG.3:
But for as long as I draw breath,
and for as long as God breathes life into me,
MSG.4:
I refuse to say one word that isn't true.
I refuse to confess to any charge that's false.
MSG.5:
There is no way I'll ever agree to your accusations.
I'll not deny my integrity even if it costs me my life.
MSG.6:
I'm holding fast to my integrity and not loosening my grip—
and, believe me, I'll never regret it.
MSG.7:
"Let my enemy be exposed as wicked!
Let my adversary be proven guilty!
MSG.8:
What hope do people without God have when life is cut short?
when God puts an end to life?
MSG.9:
Do you think God will listen to their cry for help
when disaster hits?
MSG.10:
What interest have they ever shown in the Almighty?
Have they ever been known to pray before?
MSG.11:
"I've given you a clear account of God in action,
suppressed nothing regarding God Almighty.
MSG.12:
The evidence is right before you. You can all see it for yourselves,
so why do you keep talking nonsense?

"I'll quote your own words back to you:
" 'This is how God treats the wicked,
this is what evil people can expect from God Almighty:
MSG.14:
Their children—all of them—will die violent deaths;
they'll never have enough bread to put on the table.
MSG.15:
They'll be wiped out by the plague,
and none of the widows will shed a tear when they're gone.
MSG.16:
Even if they make a lot of money
and are resplendent in the latest fashions,
MSG.17:
It's the good who will end up wearing the clothes
and the decent who will divide up the money.
MSG.18:
They build elaborate houses
that won't survive a single winter.
MSG.19:
They go to bed wealthy
and wake up poor.
MSG.20:
Terrors pour in on them like flash floods—
a tornado snatches them away in the middle of the night,
MSG.21:
A cyclone sweeps them up—gone!
Not a trace of them left, not even a footprint.
MSG.22:
Catastrophes relentlessly pursue them;
they run this way and that, but there's no place to hide—
MSG.23:
Pummeled by the weather,
blown to kingdom come by the storm.'

NET.1: And Job took up his discourse again:
NET.2: “As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice, the Almighty, who has made my life bitter —
NET.3: for while my spirit is still in me, and the breath from God is in my nostrils,
NET.4: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will whisper no deceit.
NET.5: I will never declare that you three are in the right; until I die, I will not set aside my integrity!
NET.6: I will maintain my righteousness and never let it go; my conscience will not reproach me for as long as I live.
NET.7: “May my enemy be like the wicked, my adversary like the unrighteous.
NET.8: For what hope does the godless have when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
NET.9: Does God listen to his cry when distress overtakes him?
NET.10: Will he find delight in the Almighty? Will he call out to God at all times?
NET.11: I will teach you about the power of God; What is on the Almighty’s mind I will not conceal.
NET.12: If you yourselves have all seen this, Why in the world do you continue this meaningless talk?
NET.13: This is the portion of the wicked man allotted by God, the inheritance that evildoers receive from the Almighty.
NET.14: If his children increase — it is for the sword! His offspring never have enough to eat.
NET.15: Those who survive him are buried by the plague, and their widows do not mourn for them.
NET.16: If he piles up silver like dust and stores up clothing like mounds of clay,
NET.17: what he stores up a righteous man will wear, and an innocent man will inherit his silver.
NET.18: The house he builds is as fragile as a moth’s cocoon, like a hut that a watchman has made.
NET.19: He goes to bed wealthy, but will do so no more. When he opens his eyes, it is all gone.
NET.20: Terrors overwhelm him like a flood; at night a whirlwind carries him off.
NET.21: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
NET.22: It hurls itself against him without pity as he flees headlong from its power.
NET.23: It claps its hands at him in derision and hisses him away from his place.
